## Image to video

In Video, choose **Add starting image** and select a still PNG, JPEG or WebP. Pick the output frame and length, optionally describe the motion, and generate. Workbench orients the photo, center-crops a private copy to the selected frame and uses it to condition the Wan model. The original stays untouched. The photo and sampling choice survive closing the page. Text-only prompts also work.

Fast uses 12 sampling steps, and Standard uses 16. On a 12 GB RTX 3060, one two-second, 704 × 1280 image animation took 123.1 seconds in Standard and 108.1 seconds in Fast, with the same photo, model, prompt and seed. These timings include local startup and MP4 verification. A separate text-only Fast portrait took 121.8 seconds. Timing varies by shot and machine.

The packaged Windows app generated a four-second image-conditioned portrait in 204.9 seconds. We checked playback, verified export, source similarity in the opening frame, motion across the clip, all three image formats and JPEG orientation. Five UI checks and 20 native video tests passed. Two fixture-writing tests were ignored by the native harness.
